segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Two storms · Hormuz talks stall · A crypto exchange reopens
bullets: Nolo builds toward a major hurricane as the nor'easter lingers
Trump rejects Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
Bitget starts paying withdrawals back out this week
A measles death, and two baseball races end today

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Sunday, September twenty-seventh.
Today: a hurricane building strength south of Hawaii, a nor'easter that won't let go of the Northeast, and Iran's latest offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, rejected.
Plus a crypto exchange starts giving money back, a first measles death of the year, and two Major League Baseball division races come down to the very last day. Let's get to it.

segments.strap: HURRICANE NOLO BUILDS AS NOR'EASTER LINGERS IN THE NORTHEAST
segments.headline: Two storms, still going

graphic.title: One storm building, one storm staying
bullets: Nolo forecast to reach major-hurricane strength Monday, south of Hawaii
Could be the third 2026 hurricane to pass within fifty miles of the islands
Nor'easter: coastal flooding in Jersey Shore towns, low-lying New York City streets
80,000-plus still without power in the Northeast and Connecticut

lines.text: We start again with the weather, because it's still the weekend's biggest story.

In the Pacific, Hurricane Nolo is moving slowly west, away from Hawaii's Big Island, at around a hundred miles an hour. The Hurricane Center expects it to keep strengthening and reach major-hurricane force by Monday, though it should stay south of the islands.

That would make Nolo the third hurricane this year to pass within fifty miles of Hawaii. Watches have eased, but high wind warnings remain, and forecasters still say up to thirty-five inches of rain could bring flooding and mudslides to the Big Island and eastern Maui.

Back on the mainland, that nor'easter is on day two. Coastal flood and high wind warnings remain in effect for the Jersey Shore, Long Island and eastern Connecticut into Monday, and more than eighty thousand customers, including in New York City, are still without power.

segments.strap: TRUMP REJECTS IRAN'S SEVEN-DAY PLAN TO REOPEN HORMUZ
segments.headline: A Hormuz proposal, turned down

graphic.title: Talks stall, ships still moving
bullets: Iran's plan: reopen Hormuz within seven days if the U.S. lifts its blockade and sanctions
Trump says he rejected it; Iran says it's still waiting for a formal answer
Meanwhile, the U.S. military is now escorting ships through the strait by daylight

lines.text: Iran had proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, in exchange for the U.S. releasing frozen funds, lifting oil sanctions, and ending its blockade of Iranian ports.

President Trump told reporters Saturday he turned it down. Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, says Tehran has seen an initial reaction but is still waiting, through mediators, for what he called Washington's definitive answer.

That's a claim from Tehran, not a joint statement, so treat it as one side's account. What is confirmed: the U.S. military is now guiding ships through Hormuz during daylight hours, and Fortune reports oil volume leaving the Gulf has roughly doubled.
So talks are stuck, but the ships are moving more than they were. Two different tracks, and they're not moving at the same speed.

segments.strap: BITGET STARTS PAYING WITHDRAWALS BACK OUT THIS WEEK
segments.headline: A hacked exchange starts to reopen

graphic.title: Bitget's restart schedule
bullets: Bitcoin withdrawals resume Monday
Ethereum networks Tuesday, Tether networks Wednesday
Everything else, plus cash and peer-to-peer, by Friday

lines.text: An update on that crypto exchange hack we told you about: Bitget says three hundred eighty-seven million, five hundred thousand dollars moved out to attacker-controlled wallets before it caught the breach.
The exchange says the vulnerability is now fixed and no further unauthorized transfers are possible. It's bringing withdrawals back in stages, starting with Bitcoin tomorrow.
Ethereum networks follow the day after, Tether the day after that, and everything else, including cash and peer-to-peer transfers, by this Friday.

segments.strap: CDC CONFIRMS FIRST U.S. MEASLES DEATH OF THE YEAR
segments.headline: A first death, and a dispute over the count

graphic.title: Measles in 2026
bullets: 47 jurisdictions, 40 outbreaks reporting
Pennsylvania reports four measles-associated deaths
HHS Secretary Kennedy disputes that, says only one was measles
Vaccination coverage down from 95.2% before the pandemic

lines.text: The Centers for Disease Control has confirmed the country's first measles-related death of the year. The state has not been disclosed. Nationally, there are now three thousand, six hundred fifty-nine confirmed cases, up about five and a half percent from last week.

In Pennsylvania alone, health officials count four measles-associated deaths. But Health and Human Services Secretary Kennedy disputes that, saying only one of those was actually measles. That's a real disagreement between a state health department and the federal government.

Behind both numbers: kindergarten vaccination coverage has fallen from just over ninety-five percent before the pandemic to just over ninety-two percent now. Public health researchers put roughly two hundred eighty thousand kindergartners at higher risk because of that gap.

segments.strap: GUARDIANS CLINCH AS ASTROS, RANGERS PLAY FOR IT ALL TODAY
segments.headline: Baseball's final day

graphic.title: Down to the wire
bullets: Guardians clinch a third straight AL Central title and a first-round bye
Astros and Rangers tied in the AL West, winner decided today
Astros' Carlos Correa done for the year, ankle surgery
Commanders' Jayden Daniels, Jets' Fitzpatrick and Taylor all out

lines.text: Sports. Cleveland's already popping corks: the Guardians beat the Royals eleven to five Saturday, clinching their third straight American League Central title and a first-round playoff bye.

Out west, it's still open. The Rangers and Astros both sit at eighty and eighty-one after Saturday's games, so today's finale in the AL West decides it, with Houston holding the tiebreaker if both teams finish tied. Neither club can finish better than five hundred this year.
Tough day for Houston either way: shortstop Carlos Correa is done for the season after ankle tendon surgery.
In football, Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels is officially out with an elbow injury, and the Jets will be without safety Minkah Fitzpatrick and tight end Mason Taylor today.

segments.strap: JOBS REPORT, INFLATION DATA HEADLINE A BIG WEEK AHEAD
segments.headline: The week ahead, economically

graphic.title: This week's data
bullets: Tuesday: consumer confidence, August job openings
Wednesday: August inflation reading, second GDP revision
Friday: September jobs report
No shutdown risk — government funded through December 11th

lines.text: A look ahead, since markets were closed this weekend. Tuesday brings the Conference Board's consumer confidence reading and August job openings. Wednesday brings the Fed's preferred inflation gauge and the third estimate of second-quarter growth.
And Friday, the big one: the September jobs report.
One thing that won't complicate any of it: no shutdown risk. Congress funded the government through December eleventh back on September first, so this week's data comes out on schedule.
